_comment: One job per STRIP — the whole strip as one image, for the concept run. Run with comic_render.py --provider runway|google|openai.

jobs.title: Drift Wood #2 · the vending machine
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 17, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: A dollar goes in. Nothing comes out. Wood takes it personally, then philosophically. Panel 1: a gaunt teenage boy in an oversized wool overcoat carefully feeding a limp dollar bill into a school vending machine, harsh fluorescent light (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: close-up inside a vending machine window, the metal coil turned and a bag of chips hanging caught on the edge, not falling. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: a teenage boy pressing his forehead and both hands against the glass of a vending machine while a student passes behind him (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "This machine has taken my dollar and given me a lesson about desire. That is not what I asked for.". Panel 4: a teenage boy alone at a vending machine, his face reflected in the glass beside a hanging bag of chips, empty cafeteria behind, heavy black spotting (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says, in a small balloon, "Fine. Keep it. I'll write about you.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
